p.b: DOES NOT — and that is correct

the platform has given them
nothing to do: no socket,
no offer, no call

live socket, not a fact (B7)

AND its attestation_count (D61)

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

D52's exclusion set

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
the frozen snapshot
so the brief still renders (D42)

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the rule underneath both columns.
The PERSON's axis survives, because they said it.
The PLATFORM's axis does not, because after a restart
the platform genuinely knows nothing. That is what the
two axes were for all along (D33) — this is the first
time the distinction had to do real work.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
and an absence can be data.
No wrap-up row means the call was never wrapped up,
which is TRUE and useful. D45 refuses to auto-save
precisely so that stays true — a restore that invented
one would replace a fact with a fabrication.
